doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The names Foreststorn and Chico
summary: Foreststorn is an Indian name his mother gave him, Chico came to replace it, and he says little about his secretive parents or his Texan father.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Okay. Let’s go back before this first reel is out. Let’s go back to the origin of your name Foreststorn, and if you can discuss that and then discuss how you got the moniker Chico.
Foreststorn is an Indian name.
What tribe?
Well, Apache.
Apache, Foreststorn.
La buskie (?), you know, trees, the forest. And it became easier for people to say Chico, which meant little boy, then Foreststorn.
And who named you?
My mother.
Your mother named you.
My mother.
So was she of Apache descent?
Like I said, man, she was everything. She was all the losers.
Where was your father originally from? I know LA but -­
No, he was originally from Austin, Texas.
Texas, okay.
Very interesting history but I don’t want to go into that.
Why not?
I don’t want to go into it.
Okay, that’s your prerogative. It might be historical.
No, man, well it’s not beautiful. It’s cool, man.
How about your mother?
I know very little about her also. They were very quiet, very secretive, you know.
But as long as you were in the house your parents were together?
Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah, man, oh, yeah.
